designs.title: Pisa
designs.why: Clean, confident one-ink line art that reads instantly from 3 m: perforated stamp edge, double frame, spaced serif PISA, and the 3.97 degree lean used as the denomination is a smart quiet joke. Works on white and inverts well on black. Production concerns: the gallery tiers are dense, with many white gaps only about 2 px (roughly 0.4 mm at print size) between columns and arch rings. These will fill in on a 156-ish mesh, and worse with an underbased white on the black tee, so the mid-tower risks turning into dark bands. A tapering hairline white wedge under the left side of the base also closes to nothing and will plug. The 3.97 numerals are kerned tight around the period. Overall it is a solid but expected stamp-souvenir composition for $50.
designs.fix: Simplify the tower galleries for the screen: drop roughly every other column per tier and open all counters and gaps to at least 0.5-0.6 mm (about 3-4 px at this file size). Also set the base flat on the ground line so there is no tapering sliver, which keeps the arcades crisp on both tees.
